facts.text: Spanish colonists first documented San Mateo as part of the Rancho de las Pulgas and Rancho San Mateo, with records kept at Mission Dolores.
Downtown San Mateo remains a hub for the Japanese‑American community, featuring numerous Japanese restaurants and shops.
San Mateo’s first public library opened in 1883, and Library Hall was finished in 1885, sharing the building with other city offices.
American cargo ships once called the bay’s shoreline Big Coyote, but today Coyote Point hosts CuriOdyssey, a leading natural‑history museum and wildlife center.
San Mateo’s coastal influence keeps the climate comfortable and rarely hot, making summer drives pleasantly mild.
The San Mateo County History Museum, housed in a historic downtown building, chronicles the region’s earliest times through vivid exhibits.
